A.biggest_strength: Separating pre-activations (z) and activations (h) into distinct graph nodes and pairing the graph with geometric tangent-slope plots, outer-product matrix grids, and a responsive vertical mobile layout makes every mechanism of backpropagation visually concrete.
A.biggest_weakness: The gradient update scene only computes a single step from the preset weights rather than letting the reader click repeatedly to watch loss converge over multiple iterations (and the sigmoid slope label slightly overlaps the curve).

B.biggest_strength: Interactive multi-step gradient descent ("Take a gradient step") with a live loss sparkline and live finite-difference numerical verification table that updates as parameters evolve.
B.biggest_weakness: The network diagram relies on multi-line text lists inside large node boxes rather than visual mechanisms, and its fixed 820px minimum width severely clips the graph on phone screens.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is a much stronger visual explainer because it shows the actual mechanisms of backpropagation—separating linear pre-activations (z) and nonlinear activations (h) into distinct nodes connected by a local-slope edge, plotting the loss and sigmoid curves with live tangent slopes, demonstrating gradient summation where paths merge at fan-out nodes, and visualizing weight gradients as outer-product matrices. Page A also reflows into a dedicated top-to-bottom graph at phone width so the entire network remains visible, whereas Page B crams six lines of equations into each node box, keeps a confusing un-legended yellow parameter trace permanently highlighted across all steps, and clips more than half the SVG horizontally on mobile.
